info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package x402 is pay-per-request over HTTP 402: quote a price, take the payment, serve the resource.

get.summary: Lists the flat fees this deployment sells per request over x402: one function invoke, one agent run, one provisioned resource of each kind.
get.description:
Lists the flat fees this deployment sells per request over x402: one
function invoke, one agent run, one provisioned resource of each kind. Each row
is the route's own fee knob, paid into the platform's wallet, and carries the
exact terms that route's 402 challenge states, so a client can sign before it
is refused.

A payment is made on the route itself: the client calls it with the signed
PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header, is served once, and reads the receipt on
PAYMENT-RESPONSE. The payer must be signed in, and the payment is drawn from
its Hanzo wallet, which must cover the fee. The payment is settled only once the
call is done and billable, so a call that fails costs nothing. A fee whose knob
is zero is free and is not listed; with no platform wallet configured the table
is empty.

get.summary: Answers one fee's x402 challenge: always 402, with the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header the fee's route sends an unfunded caller, and the same row the price table lists as the body.
get.description:
Answers one fee's x402 challenge: always 402, with the PAYMENT-REQUIRED
header the fee's route sends an unfunded caller, and the same row the price
table lists as the body.

It sells nothing itself. A payment sent here is never settled; it is made on
the route the row names, where it buys one call. An unknown product, or one
not sold here, is 404.

parameters.name: product
parameters.description: Product is the fee's product name, e.g. function.invoke or provision.sql.

get.summary: Lists the caller's x402 receipts, newest first: as payer, what its wallet paid; as payee, what its org was paid — each settled payment with what it bought, both parties, the exact amount and when.
get.description:
Lists the caller's x402 receipts, newest first: as payer, what its
wallet paid; as payee, what its org was paid — each settled payment with what it
bought, both parties, the exact amount and when. A payer is the caller's own
account, which for a SuperAdmin inspecting another org is still its own and for
a member of the signup org is their own wallet, never the org's; a payee is the
caller's own org. An unsettled claim is not a receipt and is never listed.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
Role is payer — what the caller's org paid — or payee — what it was paid.
Payer when empty.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description:
Year keeps the calendar year (UTC) the payments settled in. Zero keeps
every year.

get.summary: Reads one x402 payment receipt by id.
get.description:
Reads one x402 payment receipt by id.

It is scoped to the caller's own account — the wallet that was drawn, in the
books that hold it — so one tenant can never read another's settlement, nor one
member of the signup org another's, and an id that exists but belongs to
somebody else is a 404 exactly like one that does not exist. A caller with no
billable identity is refused outright.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the settlement id from the URL — the deterministic keccak(from|nonce)
key an x402 receipt is issued under (the `id` field of a Receipt, and the
`transaction` of the SettlementResponse on the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header a paid
request answers with).

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

assetTransferMethod.description:
AssetTransferMethod is how the token moves: "eip3009", its own
transferWithAuthorization. Absent means eip3009.

name.description: Name is the token's EIP-712 domain name, e.g. "USD Coin".

version.description: Version is the token's EIP-712 domain version, e.g. "2".

amount.description: Amount is the price in atomic units of Asset, as a decimal string.

asset.description: Asset is the token contract address, which must implement EIP-3009.

extra.description: Extra is the token's EIP-712 domain the authorization is signed over.

maxTimeoutSeconds.description: MaxTimeoutSeconds is how long the client has to complete the payment.

network.description: Network is the CAIP-2 identifier of the chain, e.g. "eip155:8453".

scheme.description:
Scheme is how the payment is made: "exact", the buyer authorizing exactly
Amount. It is the only scheme implemented.

amount.description:
Amount is what actually moved, as an exact 18-decimal-place USD string. It
is NOT the atomic-unit figure the client signed: the challenge quotes the
asset's own units (USDC's 6 dp) and truncates to fit them, while the ledger
moves this exact value.

category.description:
Category is what the payment was for — service, goods, transfer or royalty
— as the price table said it: a tool call is a service, a job is what its
parties agreed.

from.description:
From is the payer's EVM address: the account that signed the EIP-3009
authorization, recovered from the signature rather than taken on trust.

id.description:
ID is the settle-once key: "x402_" + keccak(from|nonce) in hex. It is
DERIVED, not minted, so a client that re-submits the same authorization
addresses the same settlement and is served again for free rather than
charged twice. It is also the id GET /v1/x402/settlements/:id takes.

network.description:
Network is the CAIP-2 identifier the payment was settled under, e.g.
"eip155:36963". Its eip155 reference is the chain id in the EIP-712 domain
the payer signed, so it is not a label — changing it invalidates the
signature.

nonce.description:
Nonce is the client-chosen nonce from the authorization, hex — up to 32
bytes, left-padded to the contract's bytes32. It is the replay anchor: the
token contract refuses a second on-chain transfer for one (from, nonce), and
this rail refuses a second settlement for the same pair, so a ledger
settlement inherits the identical guarantee.

payee.description:
Payee is the recipient's EVM address — the `payTo` the challenge advertised
and the authorization named. A payment to any other address never settles.

payeeOrg.description:
PayeeOrg is the tenant that owns the recipient wallet, resolved at
settlement. It is who got PAID, as Payer is who paid.

payer.description:
Payer is the payer ORG — the tenant whose ledger was debited — and not an
address. It is the org the request was authenticated as, so it answers who
is billed, which the payer address alone cannot.

resource.description:
Resource is what was paid for, in the same spelling the price table and the
challenge used: the request path for a priced route, "tool:<id>" for a
priced tool.

settledAt.description:
SettledAt is when this settlement was CLAIMED, in unix seconds — the moment
the authorization was accepted, which is also the moment the time window it
carried stopped applying. A settlement finished later by reconciliation
keeps this instant.

settledVia.description:
SettledVia is which rail moved the money: "ledger", the live default, or
"chain" when the authorization is broadcast. Those two values and no others.

txHash.description:
TxHash is the chain transaction hash, present only for a "chain"
settlement. Empty on a ledger settlement — that is the normal case today,
and it means the money moved without a chain, not that it failed. The
wire's PAYMENT-RESPONSE `transaction` falls back to ID when this is empty.

accepts.description: Accepts is how the fee may be paid, as the route's challenge states it.

method.description: Method is the method of the route the fee buys one call of.

path.description:
Path is that route. A payment is sent there, on PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, never
here.

price.description: Price is the fee in US dollars, exactly.

product.description: Product names the fee: function.invoke, agent.run, provision.<kind>.

resource.description:
Resource is the fee's x402 resource: what a challenge names and a payment
is settled for.

summary.description: Summary says what one payment buys.

prices.description:
Prices is one row per fee for sale; a fee that is free or not sold here is
absent.

x402Version.description: X402Version is the protocol version the terms are stated in.

error.description: Error says the fee is paid on its route, and how.

fee.description: Fee is the fee's row, as the price table lists it.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
